title: A Thorn for the Salt Again
premise: When the border wards of Saltmere collapse and the stars go dark in a single night, Edmund Underhill — last charm-seller of the outlawed Guild of Small Mercies — discovers the wards were fed by souls the court beneath the mountain quietly bought over a century. Among them is the soul of his mentor, sold to pay the guild's debts before Edmund ever knew her. With a disgraced ward-warden, a debt-collector who defected, and a child who remembers being a star, Edmund descends to bargain, steal, and finally fight for a soul the law says belongs to the crown. He wins it back at the cost of his own name in the guild ledger, and the guild ends so its last mercy can live on outside any law.
about_author: Wendell Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging debt ledgers from defunct trade guilds before turning to fiction. They write about small magics, large bureaucracies, and the people caught between the two.

chapters.title: The Last Charm on Cordwainer Street
chapters.summary: Edmund Underhill sells a luck-knot to a fisherman's widow, hiding his guild mark as city wardens pass. His POV establishes the quiet desperation of outlawed magic and the guild reduced to three members. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as routine.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: At the guildhouse, Edmund and old Master Quillon audit a ledger that doesn't balance — a page torn out, debts marked paid in a currency neither recognizes. POV alternates to Quillon, who recognizes the currency and says nothing. Emotional beat: dread beneath domestic warmth.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: The border wards fail with a sound like a bell underwater; every star vanishes at once. Edmund watches the sky from the roof, and a child falls out of the dark onto the tiles — unharmed, glowing faintly. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What the Warden Knew
chapters.summary: Disgraced ward-warden Sera Voss arrives hunting the fallen child, but defects when she sees the wards weren't broken — they were spent. She reveals souls have been sold beneath the mountain for a century. Emotional beat: bitter vindication.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers Being Bright
chapters.summary: The child, Wren, speaks in fragments of starlight and names the mountain court as the place she was 'put away.' Edmund realizes the torn ledger page matches her memories. Emotional beat: tenderness toward something not entirely human.

chapters.title: A Debt Collector Changes Sides
chapters.summary: Harrow, the court's own debt-collector, comes to collect Wren and instead reads Edmund's ledger — and finds his own brother's name among the sold. He offers passage beneath the mountain. Emotional beat: guilt weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Quillon's Confession
chapters.summary: Quillon admits he sold a soul decades ago to keep the guild alive — the mentor's soul, Edmund's teacher, Mother Aldsey. Edmund's grief turns to fury; the guild's survival was bought with its own heart. Emotional beat: betrayal and forgiveness beginning in the same breath.

chapters.title: Down the Salt Road
chapters.summary: The five leave the dying city as the first unnatural snow falls, traveling the old salt road through wards gone feral. Wren keeps them safe from the wards that still recognize starlight. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Inn at the Withered Ford
chapters.summary: At an inn where no one ages, the party learns other souls have escaped and are hiding in the walls. Harrow must decide whether to hunt or shelter them; he shelters them. Emotional beat: mercy as a choice, not an instinct.

chapters.title: Wardens on the Road
chapters.summary: City wardens, led by Sera's former partner Cade, catch up demanding Wren. Sera fights him off but is wounded; Edmund uses forbidden magic openly for the first time in ten years. Emotional beat: the cost of becoming visible.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: They descend through the salt mines into the court — a cathedral of ledger-halls where souls hang like lamps. Edmund sees Aldsey's light and nearly breaks cover reaching for it. Emotional beat: awe and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Audience with the Tallyman
chapters.summary: The Tallyman, the court's patient accountant-king, offers a bargain: one soul returned for one freely given. He shows Edmund the guild's whole history written in his own hand. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as fairness.

chapters.title: Harrow Pays His Brother's Debt
chapters.summary: Harrow secretly offers himself for his brother, but the Tallyman refuses — a debt-collector's soul is already collateral. Harrow instead steals the key to the lamp-vaults. Emotional beat: loyalty outgrowing its contract.

chapters.title: The Vault of Lamps
chapters.summary: The theft begins: Sera unmakes the vault wards from inside, Wren's starlight hides them, and Edmund lifts Aldsey's lamp. An alarm of tolling bells fills the mountain. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Winter Falls All at Once
chapters.summary: The Tallyman releases the hoarded winter early; the long night begins above and the mountain begins to seal. The party runs through collapsing halls as the snow buries the salt road behind them. Emotional beat: flight with no way back.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Trapped at the last gate, Edmund learns the vault key works only for a guild member in good standing. He signs the ledger with his own name — erasing himself from the guild to open the way. Emotional beat: identity surrendered for love.

chapters.title: Aldsey Wakes
chapters.summary: Outside, in the blinding snow, they open the lamp. Aldsey returns diminished, starless, human — and remembers Edmund, though he has no guild name for her to greet him by. Emotional beat: reunion that aches as much as it heals.

chapters.title: The Tallyman's Reckoning
chapters.summary: The Tallyman emerges to reclaim his property, but Wren stands before him — and he kneels, recognizing the first soul he ever took. She forgives him, which unmakes his claim to any of them. Emotional beat: mercy as the sharpest justice.

chapters.title: Stars Return
chapters.summary: Wren releases the stolen light in the lamps back to the sky; stars return one by one over the buried mountain. The escaped souls from the inn choose to stay in the world, embodied and free. Emotional beat: restoration without forgetting.

chapters.title: The Guild That Isn't
chapters.summary: Back in Saltmere, the guildhouse stands empty and its charter is struck from city records — officially dead. Unofficially, five people and one returned teacher begin selling small mercies again, nameless and unregistered. Emotional beat: quiet triumph.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: Edmund finds the old ledger's final page rewritten in his own erased handwriting: the guild's true record was never debts, but everyone it refused to abandon. Quillon, dying peacefully, asks to be buried under it. Emotional beat: grief braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: A Thorn for the Salt
chapters.summary: Spring comes late but comes. Edmund, now simply 'the charm-seller on Cordwainer Street,' gives Wren a luck-knot and watches her walk toward a sky that knows her. The last line: justice kept outside the law, like a thorn kept to remind the salt it once was sea. Emotional beat: hard-won peace.
